{{ElectionsAZ}}
The '''2026 Arizona gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Arizona]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Katie Hobbs]] is seeking a second term. She is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[United States House of Representatives|congressman]] [[Andy Biggs]].

[[Primary elections]] took place on July 21, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025 |title=2026 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|website= NCSL |access-date=5 August 2025}}</ref> Hobbs secured the Democratic nomination unopposed. Biggs secured the Republican nomination over congressman [[David Schweikert]] with 73.6% of the vote.<ref name=results>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-elections/arizona-governor-results|title=Arizona Governor Primary Results|work=[[NBC News]]|access-date=July 22, 2026}}</ref>  

Following the passage of Proposition 131 in the [[2022 Arizona elections|2022 elections]], this will be the first gubernatorial election in Arizona in which candidates will be required to nominate a [[running mate]] for the newly established position of [[Lieutenant Governor of Arizona|lieutenant governor]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Arizona will elect its first lieutenant governor in 2026. What to know about the role |first=Stacey |last=Barchenger |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |date=September 21, 2023 |access-date=October 14, 2024 |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/arizona/2023/09/21/arizona-will-elect-its-first-lieutenant-governor-in-2026-what-to-know/70848159007/}}</ref> This will be one of five Democratic-held governorships up for election in 2026 in a state that [[Donald Trump]] won in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]].
{{toclimit|3}}

== Background ==
Arizona is considered to be a [[purple state]] at both the federal and statewide level. After [[Joe Biden]] carried the state narrowly in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Arizona|2020 presidential election]],<ref>[https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/12/politics/biden-wins-arizona Biden carries Arizona, flipping a longtime Republican stronghold], CNN, November 13, 2020</ref> [[Donald Trump]] carried the state of Arizona by 5.5 points in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Arizona|2024 presidential election]].<ref>[https://news.sky.com/story/us-election-how-big-a-win-was-this-for-donald-trump-13250701 US election: How big a win was this for Donald Trump?], Sky News, January 20, 2025</ref> Democrats control both [[U.S. Senate]] seats in Arizona<ref>[https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/12/democrat-gallego-wins-arizona-senate-race-defining-republican-majority Democrat Gallego wins Arizona, Republicans hold 53-47 US Senate majority], Al Jazeera, November 12, 2024</ref><ref>[https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/mark-kelly-wins-senate-race-in-arizona Mark Kelly wins Senate race in Arizona], PBS, November 12, 2022</ref> and hold the governorship, secretary of state office, and attorney general office.<ref>[https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-arizona-governor-hobbs-ceadb2bf55f1d5ec4760f423f1af0204 Hobbs wins Arizona governor's race, flipping state for Dems], AP News, November 14, 2022</ref><ref>[https://www.multistate.us/insider/2024/11/6/post-election-republicans-add-to-strong-hold-of-state-governments Post-Election: Republicans Add to Strong Hold of State Governments], MultiState.US, November 6, 2024</ref> Meanwhile, Republicans maintain a majority in the [[Arizona Senate]] and [[Arizona House of Representatives]],<ref>[https://coppercourier.com/2024/11/20/arizona-legislature-republican-2025/ Republicans maintain total control of the Arizona Legislature. Here's what you need to know.], The Copper Courier, November 20, 2024</ref> and control 6 of the 9 [[U.S. House of Representatives|House of Representatives seats]] in the state.<ref>[https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/11/05/arizona-congressional-races-election-results/75904496007/ Republicans keep 6-3 majority in Arizona's US House delegation], AZ Central, November 13, 2024</ref> Democrats have characterized this race as key to establishing a Democratic [[Government trifecta|trifecta]] in Arizona for the first time in 60 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Romo |first=Renee |date=2025-12-12 |title=Democrats hoping for Arizona legislature trifecta |url=https://www.kold.com/2025/12/12/democrats-hoping-arizona-legislature-trifecta/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=[[KOLD-TV|KOLD]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Green primary==
===Background===
The [[Green Party of Arizona]] disavowed candidate Risa Lombardo, accusing her of being a Republican running to draw votes from Katie Hobbs. Lombardo, a former precinct committee member for the [[Arizona Republican Party]] and wife of a Republican activist, denied the accusations. Her campaign received services from firms and attorneys with connections to Republicans. The party supported a write-in candidate in the July 21st primary, but Lombardo obtained the nomination.<ref name="Lombardo1">{{cite news |last1=Sievers |first1=Caitlin |title=‘Sham’ Green Party candidates tied to GOP machine as they funnel cash to a mystery company |url=https://azmirror.com/2026/07/27/sham-green-party-candidates-tied-to-gop-machine-as-they-funnel-cash-to-a-mystery-company/ |access-date=September 4, 2026 |work=[[Arizona Mirror]] |date=July 27, 2026}}</ref>

In early September, it was reported that the Arizona Attorney General’s Office was investigating allegations that Lombardo's campaign, among others, had used fraudulent donations with falsified voter information to obtain public funding.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sievers |first1=Caitlin |title=Three candidates now face a criminal probe over public campaign funding fraud allegations |url=https://azmirror.com/2026/09/01/three-candidates-now-face-a-criminal-probe-over-public-campaign-funding-fraud-allegations/ |access-date=September 4, 2026 |work=[[Arizona Mirror]] |date=September 1, 2026}}</ref> 

===Candidates===
==== Nominee ====

==General election==
===Debate===
A debate was held on October 6 featuring Republican nominee Andy Biggs and No Labels nominee Teri Ann Hourihan. Governor Hobbs declined to attend. Green Party nominee Risa Lombardo had agreed to participate, but reversed course shortly before the debate.<ref name="Debate">{{cite news |last1=Evans |first1=Jordan Willow |title=Arizona No Labels Nominee Teri Ann Hourihan Faces Andy Biggs in Governor Debate |url=https://independentpoliticalreport.com/2026/10/arizona-no-labels-nominee-teri-ann-hourihan-faces-andy-biggs-in-governor-debate/ |access-date=October 13, 2026 |work=[[Independent Political Report]] |date=October 11, 2026}}</ref>
